meta.title: FrameSight: Warframe Reward Overlay for Linux, Windows, Deck
meta.description: Free, open-source Warframe companion: platinum and ducat values on the reward screen and Baro's kiosk. Native on Linux, Windows and Steam Deck. No Overwolf.

hero.pill: New: bounty and endless rotations on the Dashboard
hero.title: Know what every Warframe reward is worth.
hero.lede: FrameSight shows the platinum and ducat price of each card on the relic reward screen and at Baro Ki’Teer’s kiosk. Free, open source, and it never writes to the game.
hero.meta: No Overwolf · No account · No telemetry
hero.note: Illustrative values. In game, prices come from the warframe.market sellers who are online.
hero.platformsLabel: Made for Tenno who play on

how.label: How it works
how.title: Install, allow, open a relic.
how.installText: One installer on Windows. A package or an AppImage on Linux and the Steam Deck.
how.accessText: It reads nothing until you pick an access level. The overlays only need the screen and the game’s log.
how.playText: On the reward screen, each card shows its platinum and ducat value. Take the one that pays.

kiosk.title: Baro's Ducat Kiosk, priced in platinum.
kiosk.text: Before you trade a Prime part for ducats, see what it would sell for. Every tile gets its platinum figure, every pick lands in a sell list, and the list totals itself as it fills.
kiosk.point1: Parts of gear you have not mastered read Unmastered, with Full access
kiosk.point2: Drawn over the kiosk itself; the game never loses focus
kiosk.note: Try it: pick the tiles. Illustrative prices.
kiosk.more: More about the Ducat Kiosk overlay

tour.title: Between missions, one quiet window.
tour.text: The world's timers, a collection priced to the platinum, and sell orders that match what you actually hold.
tour.dashboardText: Cycles, fissures, the sortie, the archon hunt and Baro's next visit.
tour.collectionText: Every item with its platinum and ducat value, filtered to what is left to master.
tour.ordersText: warframe.market listings checked against what you actually hold.

bento.masteryText: A mastery checklist built from your own inventory, with Full access.
bento.relicsTitle: Relics ranked by what they pay
bento.relicsText: Farms and relics ranked by platinum per run.
bento.bountyText: Cetus, Orb Vallis and the Cambion Drift: each tier with the table it pays from.
bento.linuxTitle: Native on Linux. At home on Windows.
bento.linuxText: Proton, Wine, the Steam Deck in Desktop Mode, or one Windows installer with nothing else to set up.

access.title: You decide what it reads. Before it reads anything.
access.text: FrameSight asks for an access level the first time it opens and observes nothing until you confirm. Lower it later and everything it no longer permits stops at once.
access.label: Access level
access.overlayShort: Reads the screen and the game's log
access.companionGives: The Dashboard, the collection from a snapshot, prices, relics, farming and warframe.market orders.
access.companionSends: Nothing about you. Prices, the item catalogue and world state are downloaded. warframe.market sees you only if you link it.
access.overlayReads: The screen, and the game's log file EE.log to know when a reward screen opens. Never the game's memory.
access.overlayGives: Everything in Companion, plus the reward overlay and the Ducat Kiosk overlay.
access.overlaySends: Nothing more than Companion. The screen is read on your machine with Tesseract.
access.fullReads: Everything in Overlay, plus an account ID and nonce from the Warframe process.
access.fullGives: Automatic inventory sync, and owned, missing and mastery marks on every slip, card and kiosk tile.
access.fullSends: That ID and nonce to mobile.warframe.com's inventory endpoint, and nowhere else.
access.never: At every level: no writing to the game, no automated input, no telemetry.

download.title: Get FrameSight
download.label: Operating system
download.winText: One installer, for your user only, so no admin prompt. It carries its own text reader and fetches Microsoft's WebView2 runtime if your PC lacks it.
download.winStep1: SmartScreen warns the first time because the installer is not code-signed. Choose More info, then Run anyway.
download.winStep2: Set Warframe's Display Mode to Borderless. In exclusive fullscreen no app can draw over the game.
download.winStep3: Pick an access level when FrameSight opens. Nothing observes the game until you confirm.
download.winNote: FrameSight is developed on Linux. Windows builds are tested, but less often: if something is off, an issue on GitHub helps.
download.fedoraText: An .rpm package with a framesight command and a desktop entry. Warframe can run through Steam's Proton or Wine.
download.fedoraStepsTitle: Install it, with the text reader the overlays use
download.fedoraPoint1: Run it from a terminal, in the folder you downloaded to.
download.debianText: A .deb package with a framesight command and a desktop entry.
download.debianNote: The package needs glibc 2.39. On Ubuntu 22.04 or Debian 12, take the AppImage instead.
download.appimageText: One self-contained file, nothing to install. On the Steam Deck, switch to Desktop Mode first.
download.appimageStepsTitle: Make it runnable, then start it
download.appimagePoint1: Works back to Ubuntu 22.04 and Debian 12.
download.appimagePoint2: The reward overlay needs tesseract with its English data from your distribution.
download.foot: Every build and changelog is on the GitHub releases page. The reward reader matches English and French item names, so the game has to run in one of the two. Step-by-step guides: Linux, Steam Deck.

faq.title: Questions, answered plainly.
faq.text: Anything else lives in the repository.

items.q: Does FrameSight modify Warframe or automate anything?
items.a: No. It only reads: the screen and EE.log for the overlays, and, at Full access only, an account ID and nonce from the game process. No access level writes to the game or automates input.

items.q: Does it need Overwolf or an account?
items.a: No. FrameSight is a standalone desktop app with no account and no telemetry. Linking warframe.market is optional and only needed to manage your orders. How it compares with Overwolf apps.

items.q: Does it work on Linux and the Steam Deck?
items.a: Yes, it is developed on Linux. It reads Warframe running through Proton or Wine, and the Steam Deck runs the AppImage in Desktop Mode. See FrameSight on Linux and on the Steam Deck.

items.q: Where do the prices come from?
items.a: From warframe.market. The collection uses a daily summary served by relics.run; the reward screen prices the whole squad's relic pool from the sellers who are in game right now. Ducat values are Baro Ki'Teer's.

items.q: Why doesn't the overlay show up?
items.a: Set Warframe's Display Mode to Borderless: in exclusive fullscreen nothing can draw over the game. The reward reader also needs the game in English or French, and the access level set to Overlay or Full.
Yes, free and open source under the GPL-3.0 license. FrameSight continues TennoScope, created by Deftera186 and its contributors.
